do_more: Open titles and first lines with direct, physical second-person assertions ('Your Face...', 'Your Kids...', 'Your Brain...') instead of abstract questions.
Focus on visceral, observable physiological reactions (shock, facial freezing, laughter, eye blinks) rather than internal philosophical pondering.
Frame psychological concepts around ancient survival mechanisms, evolution, and primal brain wiring.
Keep pacing punchy and under 35 seconds to maximize loop potential, as top-retention performers thrive when viewers can finish easily.
avoid: Avoid weak yes/no inquiry titles starting with 'Can your...', 'Does your...', or 'Do you...'.
Avoid academic book titles, citation subtitles ('Reading 5', '1890 blueprint'), and dry book reviews without personal stakes.
Avoid intellectual, abstract themes like ego survival, subconscious theory, and historical eugenics.
short.title_style: Short, punchy 3-to-5 word declarative statements starting with 'Your [Body Part / Emotion]' tied to an intense physical or evolutionary reaction.
next_tests: A/B test declarative physical hooks ('Your Pupils Dilate When Lying') against question hooks ('Do your eyes give you away?') on the exact same 30s script.
Test high-urgency parenting and developmental psychology hooks ('Your Toddler Expects Danger') based on the standout success of 'Your Kids Expect Shock'.

do_more: Anchor titles to relatable visceral experiences like dreams, facial expressions, or daily personal struggles rather than abstract academic concepts.
Include recognizable household author names like Sigmund Freud or Charles Darwin directly in the title to leverage built-in search intent and curiosity.
Frame opening hooks around an immediate, mysterious physical or emotional sensation that the viewer personally experiences.
avoid: Dry academic textbook titles like 'Reading 1' or generic lecture style titles like 'What does psychoanalysis say about your mind?'
Abstract sociological questions about group opinions or social change that lack direct personal stakes for the individual viewer.
full.title_style: High-performing titles frame a highly personal, direct question about the viewer's body or subconscious mind paired with an iconic public-domain author.
next_tests: Test a visceral self-analysis title using Sigmund Freud focusing on hidden slips, secret motives, or guilt.
Test an evolution-based self-preservation question attached to Charles Darwin focusing on fear or flight responses.
